body.title: fix(bigquery): preserve reported types in unit test fixtures
body.body:
Unit-test fixtures become SQL rows whose types must match the referenced columns. The renderer previously worked from Arrow data types alone: BigQuery `GEOGRAPHY` and `JSON` both look like strings. Fixture casts also reused the type mapping for `dbt seed`, which chooses `DATETIME` for timestamp values even when the referenced column is `TIMESTAMP`.

For example, this model returns `GEOGRAPHY`, `TIMESTAMP`, and `JSON` columns:

```sql
-- models/fixture_types.sql
SELECT
  ST_GEOGPOINT(100, -37) AS location,
  TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00+00' AS created_at,
  PARSE_JSON('{"segmentCode":"HORECA"}') AS payload;
```

A unit test supplies the matching expected row:

```yaml
# models/fixture_types.yml
unit_tests:
  - name: preserves_column_types
    model: fixture_types
    given: []
    expect:
      rows:
        - location: "ST_GEOGPOINT(100, -37)"
          created_at: "2026-01-01 00:00:00+00"
          payload: '{"segmentCode":"HORECA"}'
```

Before this fix, the expected fixture row used these casts (simplified SQL):

```sql
SELECT
  CAST('ST_GEOGPOINT(100, -37)' AS STRING) AS location,
  CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00' AS DATETIME) AS created_at,
  CAST('{"segmentCode":"HORECA"}' AS STRING) AS payload;
```

The `STRING` values are incompatible with the model's `GEOGRAPHY` and `JSON` columns. The timestamp cast fails because its UTC offset is invalid for `DATETIME`.

With this fix, the same fixture uses:

```sql
SELECT
  CAST(ST_GEOGPOINT(100, -37) AS GEOGRAPHY) AS location,
  CAST('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00' AS TIMESTAMP) AS created_at,
  CAST(PARSE_JSON('{"segmentCode":"HORECA"}') AS JSON) AS payload;
```

The renderer preserves the reported BigQuery type from field metadata, including nested arrays and structs and `NUMERIC`/`BIGNUMERIC` values. Empty arrays get explicit element types. `JSON` and `GEOGRAPHY` are excluded from `ORDER BY`, which BigQuery [does not support for these types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#orderable_data_types). The fix reuses the existing type lookup and rendering paths; other adapters keep their current mappings.

Related: #13804, #14271, #14625, #15708, #15882

body.title: fix: table headers align with their column's data type instead of always right-justifying
body.body:
Resolves #13635

### Problem

`print_table()`'s `write_row` closure in `crates/dbt-agate/src/print_table.rs` unconditionally right-justified every header cell, regardless of whether the column it headed contained text or numbers. Data cells, by contrast, were justified per their own content (numeric values right-justified, text left-justified). For a text column whose header is shorter than its widest data value (e.g. header `column_name` vs. a value like `LOW_FIDELITY_INT`), this made the header's padding direction disagree with the data's, visibly shifting the header text within its cell relative to the divider and data rows below it — reported as misaligned pipes / a "single extra whitespace" in the contract-mismatch table printed when a data contract violation is detected.

### Solution

Classify each column as numeric or text once, from its data (every non-empty, non-ellipsis value parses as a number, and at least one such value exists), and justify that column's header the same way — matching the convention Python `agate` already uses (align the header to the column's type, not to whether it's a header). Data-row justification is unchanged.

Added 4 unit tests to `crates/dbt-agate/src/print_table.rs` (previously untested): the exact scenario reported in #13635, a fully-numeric column (confirms no regression for the common case), an empty table, and a mixed numeric/text column edge case.

One edge case worth flagging for reviewers: the synthetic `"..."` truncated-columns marker column previously right-justified its header (because it's a header) and now left-justifies (because it has no numeric data to infer a type from). Happy to special-case that if byte-identical output is wanted there too.

body.title: fix: ignore null dbt_project.yml keys in project config extraction
body.body:
Resolves #16290

### Problem

If a key in the `dbt_project.yml` model tree has a null value (e.g. `beta:` with no children or configs), any change to that key caused `state:modified` to select every model beneath the parent block, including unrelated siblings.

Root cause: `_project_configs` treated any non-dict value as a legacy bare config. YAML null parses as `None`, which is not a dict, so the placeholder key was copied into every sibling's `unrendered_config` and then compared by `same_contents`.

### Solution

Skip `None` values in the legacy bare-config branch so null hierarchy placeholders are not treated as config, while still supporting bare scalars (`materialized: view`) and `+`-prefixed explicit nulls (`+enabled: null`).

Adds unit regression coverage in `tests/unit/context/test_context_config.py`.
